title: Left-handed in the Ma Rainey pictures and relearning
summary: He notes he is left-handed in the Ma Rainey photographs and says it took six to eight months to get used to the right-handed trombone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Well, no, the baritone I played at the right hand.

I played the baritone right hand, see. So, I stuck it on through this many times. I got disgusted. I said, well, there's no point in going through all this. But I never, if you notice on all the old pictures with Ma Rainey, all those Ma Rainey pictures and everything, if you notice, I'm left hand. Yeah, I'm playing left hand. I never noticed. I never noticed.
I never look at that though. It's funny I would have missed it.

Well, it's not a thing that the average layman would look at. I mean, it's just something you might look at a picture and say, well, something seems wrong, but you can't quite put your hand on it. Yeah.
I never felt like it. It doesn't bother you anymore now at all, I guess. You don't even think about it. Oh, no, I don't even think about it. You never know what to look at you.
I didn't even think about it. I mean, I went through that period. It probably take me six or eight months to get the feel of it.
And then after that, I mean, it's kind of natural.
You still write, I guess, left-handed? Yeah.
